question: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Seattle, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

notes.anthropic: Seattle's flagship contemporary dealer since 1983; museum-quality shows, a deep print program and the region's most consistent art-fair and institutional presence.
notes.openai: Seattle’s leading long-established contemporary gallery, with a nationally recognized roster, sustained art-fair activity and strong museum placement.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1977; the gallery that made Northwest studio glass an international story, now balancing glass with painting and sculpture, with long-running fair participation.
notes.openai: Internationally influential in contemporary glass while maintaining a broader sculpture and painting program with major institutional reach.

notes.anthropic: Seattle–New York dealer with a polished contemporary painting and photography roster and steady Art Miami / Seattle Art Fair presence.
notes.openai: A prominent Seattle–New York gallery representing established contemporary artists across painting, photography, sculpture and installation.

notes.anthropic: Operating since 1968, one of the oldest and largest commercial spaces in the city; bridges Northwest School legacies with mid-career contemporary artists.
notes.openai: A durable regional anchor with a broad contemporary roster and particular strength in Northwest painting, sculpture and glass.

notes.anthropic: For two decades Seattle's most internationally connected program (Bunny Rogers, Claude Zervas, Robert Yoder) before closing its space in 2021; still the benchmark local dealers are measured against.
notes.openai: A rigorous contemporary program with national and international artists, regular fair participation and substantial institutional attention.

notes.anthropic: Since 1974 the Northwest's authority on works on paper, pairing antique master prints with a serious contemporary print and drawing program.
notes.openai: One of the country’s important works-on-paper dealers, combining historic print expertise with a substantial contemporary program.

notes.anthropic: Artist-run cooperative founded 1995 and the incubator for a generation of Seattle artists; still the city's most credible experimental co-op.
notes.openai: Seattle’s most consequential artist-run gallery, sustaining experimental practices and launching many artists who later gained institutional recognition.

notes.anthropic: Black art space in a family home in the Central District; nationally covered model for art, anti-displacement work and community archive.
notes.openai: A nationally noticed Black arts organization presenting exhibitions, residencies and community programs in a culturally significant neighborhood house.

notes.anthropic: Long-established Los Angeles gallery that relocated to Seattle in 2017 and later joined forces with Prographica; figurative work and drawing of national standing.
notes.openai: Known for technically accomplished figurative and narrative art, with a long record of national exhibitions and institutional placements.

notes.anthropic: The most energetic newer commercial gallery in Pioneer Square, with a diverse emerging roster and strong Seattle Art Fair visibility.
notes.openai: A well-regarded contemporary program emphasizing distinctive regional voices, material experimentation and sustained artist development.

notes.anthropic: City-run cultural space whose top-floor gallery opened with yəhaw̓; the largest publicly programmed contemporary exhibition hall outside the museums.
notes.openai: Seattle’s flagship municipal exhibition space, notable for ambitious artist-led projects and sustained emphasis on communities historically excluded from institutions.

notes.anthropic: Dawna Holloway's compact Georgetown room with an outsized critical reputation for tightly curated shows by respected Northwest artists.
notes.openai: A closely curated contemporary gallery that has become influential for introducing emerging and mid-career artists to Seattle collectors and institutions.

notes.anthropic: Leading dealer of contemporary Northwest Coast and Alaska Native art since 1979, with artists collected by major museums.
notes.openai: A major venue for contemporary Indigenous art of the Pacific Northwest Coast, representing leading carvers, glass artists and multidisciplinary practitioners.

notes.anthropic: King County's juried exhibition space; a career-launching solo slot for emerging and mid-career artists, free of commercial pressure.
notes.openai: King County’s principal public contemporary-art gallery, supporting experimental work by regional artists through exhibitions and commissions.

notes.anthropic: The region's photography hub; its gallery brings national photographers and juried surveys to Seattle audiences.
notes.openai: The region’s leading nonprofit photography venue, pairing critically engaged exhibitions with residencies, publications and public education.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1962 and Seattle's oldest continuously operating gallery; custodian of the Northwest School and its contemporary descendants.
notes.openai: A historically important Seattle gallery whose long program connects Northwest modernism with successive generations of contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Jacob Lawrence Gallery
galleries.address_hint: UW School of Art, 15th Ave NE

notes.anthropic: University of Washington's kunsthalle-style gallery; adventurous curated projects, visiting-artist shows and a link to the Jacob Lawrence legacy.
notes.openai: The University of Washington’s principal contemporary-art gallery, connecting visiting artists, research, experimental curating and emerging practices.

notes.anthropic: Long-running artist cooperative with a juried associate program; a dependable entry point for emerging Seattle artists.
notes.openai: A durable artist-run gallery providing consistent public exposure for emerging and mid-career contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1980, Seattle's veteran alternative art organization; historically the venue for the city's most provocative exhibitions and performances.
notes.openai: A pioneering Seattle contemporary-art nonprofit with decades of experimental exhibitions, installations and artist-centered programming.

notes.anthropic: Thirty-year-old downtown gallery of contemporary Northwest painting and mixed media, active in corporate and civic collections.
notes.openai: A longstanding commercial gallery with a strong collector base and an established program of contemporary painting, sculpture and mixed media.

notes.anthropic: Kirsten Anderson's gallery put Seattle at the centre of pop surrealism from 1998; closed its storefront in 2021 but shaped a whole scene.
notes.openai: Internationally known for imaginative realism, pop surrealism and technically refined figurative art, with a loyal global following.

notes.anthropic: Small artist-run venue with a conceptually rigorous, quickly rotating program that critics follow closely.
notes.openai: A focused contemporary gallery and curatorial platform presenting intellectually ambitious work by emerging and established artists.

notes.anthropic: Major Waterfront dealer in contemporary Northwest Coast Native art, representing established carvers, printmakers and weavers.
notes.openai: An important commercial platform for contemporary Northwest Coast Indigenous artists, emphasizing knowledgeable representation and cultural context.

notes.anthropic: Clean-lined contemporary program of abstraction and photo-based work by Northwest and national artists.
notes.openai: A respected contemporary gallery known for vivid figurative, narrative and materially inventive work by regional and national artists.

notes.anthropic: Contemporary Japanese and Asian-American art, including projects with Gerard Tsutakawa; long history of ambitious sculptural exhibitions.
notes.openai: A veteran gallery with a cross-disciplinary program linking contemporary visual art, science, technology and public conversation.

notes.anthropic: Commissions large-scale installations built on site in public view; has given ambitious platforms to artists such as John Grade and Lauren Iida.
Artist-run cooperative offering members annual solos; a steady incubator within the Tashiro Kaplan arts building.
notes.openai: A longstanding artist-run cooperative valued for independent programming and direct support of experimental regional practices.

notes.anthropic: Thirty-plus years of representational and narrative painting; a core stop on the First Thursday circuit and a steady supporter of regional mid-career artists.
Tariqa Waters's pop-art project space and micro-museum; playful, irreverent, and a visible platform for Black artists in Pioneer Square.
notes.openai: An independent Black-led art space known for energetic exhibitions, performances and support of artists outside conventional gallery systems.

notes.anthropic: Single-installation white box devoted to site-responsive sculpture and immersive projects — a rare non-commercial platform for ambitious three-dimensional work.
Artist-run collective since 2007 known for conceptually driven solo shows and invitational projects.
Capitol Hill's social heart for emerging and BIPOC artists; exhibitions, readings and music in one hybrid room.
notes.openai: A durable hybrid gallery and social space that has made contemporary exhibitions unusually accessible to Capitol Hill audiences.

notes.anthropic: Downtown gallery of contemporary sculpture, glass and painting with an international roster and consistent presence at major fairs.
Globally oriented program of diaspora and immigrant artists; socially engaged exhibitions with a strong community education component.
Seattle University's exhibition space, known for socially engaged curatorial projects and collaborations with local artist-organizers.
notes.openai: Seattle University’s public contemporary gallery, recognized for research-driven installations, socially engaged projects and adventurous curatorial work.

notes.anthropic: Rare dedicated venue for sound art and audio-based installation, tied to a respected artist-residency program.
notes.openai: A distinctive venue for sound art, media installation and interdisciplinary work, supported by a respected residency and production program.

notes.anthropic: Publishing-and-exhibition project blending poetry, performance and visual art; nomadic since leaving its storefront but critically visible.
notes.openai: An independent exhibition, publishing and art-book platform known for conceptually adventurous projects and strong ties to artist-led culture.

notes.anthropic: Specialist in contemporary and historic Northwest painting near Pike Place; scholarly presentation of the regional canon.
Curator-run Ballard project space known for tightly conceived group shows and support of experimental practice.
notes.openai: An intimate artist-run venue that gives installation, performance and experimental work unusual freedom and close audience engagement.

notes.anthropic: In Pike Place Market since 1985, showing Northwest landscape and figurative painters with an unusually loyal collector base.

notes.openai: The successor to ArtXchange Gallery, maintaining a globally minded program centered on diasporic, cross-cultural and socially engaged practices.

notes.anthropic: Long-running Pioneer Square gallery mixing contemporary painting, sculpture and craft-based media.
Member-run space with a well-regarded juried solo program for emerging artists.
notes.openai: An artist-run cooperative sustaining regular solo and group exhibitions in the Tashiro Kaplan arts complex.

notes.anthropic: Recent arrival with an ambitious contemporary program and fair aspirations, signalling new commercial energy on Capitol Hill.
Artist-organized space showing sharp, research-driven work by younger regional and out-of-town artists.

notes.openai: A newer gallery with an unusually accomplished roster of established Northwest artists and a polished, institutionally oriented program.

notes.anthropic: Gail Gibson's gallery was for thirty years the Northwest's most serious photography dealer; now operating privately after closing its public space.
Platform for performance, sound and time-based practice that commercial galleries rarely accommodate.
notes.openai: A flexible artist-run venue for experimental exhibitions, performance, movement and other practices poorly served by commercial galleries.

notes.anthropic: Georgetown artist-run space for installation and experimental exhibitions outside the commercial circuit.
notes.openai: A small artist-run gallery with a focused emerging-art program and an emphasis on experimentation and dialogue.
An artist-founded cultural center built on a remediated former gas station, combining contemporary exhibitions with environmental and community programming.

notes.anthropic: Artist-run gallery, shop and studio for comics, illustration and zine culture; the hub of Seattle's alt-comics community.
Historic Nihonmachi storefront showing contemporary painting, ceramics and Asian-American artists.
Long-standing home for street art, graffiti and lowbrow practice in Seattle, with international guest artists.

notes.openai: A prominent Black arts and culture organization presenting exhibitions, supporting artists and preserving the Central District’s creative legacy.

notes.anthropic: Contemporary and urban-art gallery with a strong secondary-market and editions component.

notes.openai: An Indigenous-led gallery and marketplace extending yəhaw̓ Indigenous Creatives’ influential work on visibility, economic opportunity and cultural sovereignty.

notes.anthropic: Pop-culture and illustration gallery with themed group shows that draw large young audiences.

notes.openai: An artist-run workspace and exhibition platform that supports collaborative, experimental and community-oriented contemporary projects.

notes.anthropic: Tiny, densely hung salon of small-format work by dozens of local artists; a long-lived Capitol Hill fixture.

notes.openai: The exhibition arm of Seattle’s influential mural and public-art initiative, connecting street-art practices with a permanent gallery context.

notes.anthropic: Georgetown gallery and studios showing a broad cross-section of Seattle artists; anchor of the neighborhood art walk.

notes.openai: A contemporary gallery with an accessible regional program spanning abstraction, figuration, photography and mixed media.

notes.anthropic: Vast industrial complex of artist and maker studios whose open-house exhibitions are among the city's largest public art events.

notes.openai: An artist-run venue presenting idiosyncratic, critically engaged exhibitions by emerging and established contemporary artists.
A polished gallery combining contemporary exhibitions with selected modern and secondary-market material for an established collector audience.

notes.anthropic: Influential Georgetown space for video, new media and installation in the late 2010s; shaped local expectations for time-based art.

notes.openai: A long-running Seattle gallery with a broad roster and particular visibility in painting, sculpture and studio glass.

notes.anthropic: Sierra Stinson's apartment-gallery series that gave first shows to many now-established Seattle artists.
DIY gallery, shop and music venue that defined a strand of 2010s Capitol Hill youth culture and artist community.

notes.openai: A well-established venue for contemporary Northwest artists, especially painting, drawing, sculpture and materially focused work.

notes.anthropic: Georgetown artist-run gallery praised for rigorous, curatorially framed exhibitions during its run.

notes.openai: A longstanding cooperative gallery and South Seattle cultural anchor supporting diverse regional artists and community exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Robert Yoder's by-appointment gallery, admired for pairing Seattle artists with sympathetic national figures.

notes.openai: A significant Chicano- and Latinx-centered gallery presenting politically engaged contemporary art and building cultural infrastructure in West Seattle.

notes.anthropic: Rental-and-sales gallery presenting Northwest contemporary artists to a broad museum audience; a longstanding first market for many locals.

notes.openai: A Georgetown artist collective and exhibition venue fostering cross-disciplinary projects within one of Seattle’s strongest studio communities.

notes.anthropic: West Seattle's principal contemporary gallery, programmed in dialogue with the theatre's season.
Delridge arts centre whose galleries and studios foreground youth, immigrant and community-based artists.

notes.openai: A window-based exhibition space offering continuous public access to concise, experimental installations by local and visiting artists.

notes.anthropic: Black arts institution in the Central District whose visual-art exhibitions and residencies complement its performance program.

notes.openai: A developing nonprofit contemporary gallery that provides exhibitions, residencies and professional opportunities for emerging artists.

notes.anthropic: Former immigration detention building converted into 125 artist studios with regular public open-studio exhibitions.
Grew from a landmark 200-artist exhibition into an ongoing Indigenous-led organization with studio and gallery space and public commissions.
Artist collective mounting large annual surveys of Black Northwest artists in borrowed and partner venues.
Neighborhood association gallery with a juried program that has shown north-end artists for decades.
notes.openai: A well-used community gallery that provides sustained public exhibition opportunities for artists in north Seattle.

notes.anthropic: Studio-and-gallery complex north of downtown known for its annual small-works show and support of illustrators and muralists.

notes.openai: United Indians of All Tribes Foundation’s gallery provides an important public platform for contemporary Native artists and cultural continuity.
A neighborhood-based artist space presenting exhibitions, performances and community programs in a converted former grocery store.

notes.anthropic: Japanese craft-and-art gallery in the historic Higo store, mixing contemporary ceramics and design with neighborhood history exhibits.

notes.openai: A distinctive gallery and studio community advocating for accomplished older artists who remain underrepresented in the contemporary market.

notes.anthropic: Traver's separate downtown storefront for emerging glass artists and small-scale contemporary work.

notes.openai: A long-running nonprofit gallery notable for its open-entry model and broad access for artists outside established commercial networks.

notes.anthropic: Bill and Ruth True's 2004–2012 exhibition space for their international collection; the most ambitious private contemporary venue Seattle has had.

notes.openai: The public gallery of the internationally influential comics publisher, exhibiting major cartoonists, illustrators and artists working across visual narrative.

notes.anthropic: Architect George Suyama's timber-framed hall commissioned major site-specific installations for twenty years until 2017; a benchmark for installation art in the city.

notes.openai: A youth-centered exhibition space that gives emerging artists early curatorial and professional experience within a larger music and arts institution.

notes.anthropic: Scott Lawrimore's 2006–2012 gallery was the most conceptually daring commercial space of its era and reshaped what Seattle dealers attempt.
Championed emerging Northwest artists in the 2000s and helped export them to national fairs before closing.

notes.openai: Cornish College of the Arts’ principal public gallery, presenting visiting artists, faculty projects and emerging contemporary practices.

notes.anthropic: Billy Howard's gallery (1998–2011) built the careers of numerous regional contemporary artists and set a professional standard for the market.
From 1966 to 2013 the dealer for Jacob Lawrence, Gwendolyn Knight and Michael Spafford; arguably the most historically important gallery in Seattle's history.
